I am 65 this year, and I have worked these 8 mu in Quzhou County for 45 years. I graduated from the county agricultural technical school back in 1982, so I know how to read a soil test and calculate fertilizer rates, but I am still a farmer — I do not throw money at the field unless I am sure it comes back as grain.

My wife and I manage the farm ourselves. Our son works in a factory in Handan and sends money home, so we are not desperate, but with only two of us in the field, labor is tight. I hire a combine for harvest and a no-till seeder service for maize, but for spraying and irrigation, we do it ourselves. I had my soil tested at the county agricultural station three years ago: pH 8.1, organic matter 1.6%, available phosphorus medium at 18 mg/kg, available potassium low at 95 mg/kg. That test told me I must not skip potassium, especially for the maize.

Here is how I manage this year. For winter wheat, I sow Jimai 22, an improved semi-dwarf variety I have used for six years straight. It stands well and gives me a stable 550 kg per mu. I sow 18 kg of seed per mu around October 10. Before sowing, I run the rotary tiller to break up the maize stubble and level the field. For fertilizer, I apply 16 kg of pure nitrogen per mu total — I put down 8 kg N as compound fertilizer base at sowing, then at jointing stage in late March I top-dress with urea for another 8 kg N. I apply 7 kg P₂O₅ per mu and 6 kg K₂O per mu, all as base fertilizer. I irrigate three times from my well: the wintering water in late November, the jointing water in late March, and the grain-filling water in early May. Each irrigation costs me about 35 yuan per mu in electricity to run the pump. For chemicals, I spray a herbicide once in early spring, and a fungicide once at heading stage to prevent rust — two applications total.

For summer maize, timing is everything. After wheat harvest in early June, I have maybe ten days to get the maize in the ground before I lose yield to late planting. I hire the neighbor’s no-till precision seeder and plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid at 2.5 kg per mu. This variety is tough and fills grain well. I apply 17 kg N per mu total — compound fertilizer banded at sowing, then urea side-dressed at big trumpet stage. Phosphorus is 6 kg P₂O₅ per mu and potassium is 6 kg K₂O per mu, all base. I irrigate twice: once at the 7-to-8-leaf stage and once at tasseling. If August turns dry, I might add a third at grain filling, but two is usually enough. For pesticides, I spray pre-emergence herbicide right after sowing, and one insecticide at heart-leaf stage for corn borer — two applications. I expect 650 kg per mu.

I thought about cutting my nitrogen rate because the county extension talks about reducing chemical fertilizer use. But last year, my neighbor Liu cut his wheat nitrogen from 15 kg to 10 kg per mu and lost nearly 80 kg in yield. At 2.4 yuan per kg for wheat, that is 192 yuan lost to save maybe 40 yuan in urea. I am not making that mistake. I would rather spend an extra 200 yuan on fertilizer across the whole 8 mu than risk losing over 1,000 yuan in grain. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting a little fertilizer is just a cost of doing business.
